assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a single superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon, giving controllable, readable quantum devices; it is the architecture underlying dispersive readout, gates and most present superconducting processors. It is a clean new regime (strong coupling in a circuit) and the enabling platform for a large field, which I weigh as foundational physics rather than as an application.
assessment.attribution: The proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf 2004) and first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al. 2004) are tightly linked, so a theory-plus-experiment pairing is natural. Girvin and Huang are not in the supplied credit, so the theory share is unresolved; the credited trio is defensible but a three-person cap is tight.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in dozens of laboratories over two decades and stable in interpretation. Timing is good, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic tunnelling in circuits already recognised part of this platform, so overlap must be weighed.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize and the possibility the committee sees circuit QED as already partly covered.
Missing credit for Girvin and others on the theory side.
I work in this area and am close to several of these groups, so my judgement may be biased and recusal rules may apply.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and quantum control of macroscopic mechanical oscillators (sideband cooling, squeezing, entanglement, strong coupling) opened a new regime in which massive objects are prepared and measured in quantum states. This is clean, physically transparent experimental work with a clear foundational message about quantum mechanics at larger scales.
assessment.attribution: Several groups made near-simultaneous decisive advances: Teufel (microwave circuit electromechanics ground state), Cleland (quantum acoustics and phonon-qubit work), Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer (cavity optomechanics), Painter (optomechanical crystals). Choosing three involves a genuinely arbitrary cut; I favour Teufel, Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer as the broadest and most foundational set.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in optical, microwave and acoustic platforms, so the core results are robust. The field is still evolving toward applications such as sensing and transduction, but the discovery itself is mature.
uncertainties: Five credited names compete for three slots and attribution is contested.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2025 prize and earlier laureates' work on trapped-ion and optical cooling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates and Blatt's experimental realisations established the first fully controllable, high-fidelity quantum processors, and fixed concepts (gates via collective motion, entangling operations, digital quantum simulation) now used throughout the field.
assessment.attribution: Theory by Cirac and Zoller, experimental leadership by Blatt is a clear and balanced configuration. Wineland (already a laureate) and groups such as Monroe and Wineland-related work complicate the experimental credit, and Monroe is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of experimental confirmation across many laboratories. Timing is mature; some may argue the Wineland-Haroche prize already covered the core control of single quantum systems.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for measuring and manipulating single quantum systems.
Experimental credit beyond Blatt (for example Monroe) is not in the supplied names.
B047 appears to be a near-duplicate of this candidate with the same names; I rank only one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect, topological insulators and the quantum anomalous Hall effect established topology as an organising principle of band insulators with robust edge states. The ideas are original and confirmed across many materials, with lasting conceptual impact beyond condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical foundation, Molenkamp the first experimental quantum spin Hall realisation in HgTe, and Xue the quantum anomalous Hall experiment. Mele, Hasan and Zhang, Bernevig and others also made decisive contributions that this compound candidate (and B018) partly split. Zhang has died, which constrains the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with a large body of independent confirmation. The compound nature (QSH, 3D TI, QAH) means different parts may deserve different recognition.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit between Kane, Mele, Hasan, Molenkamp and Xue; B018 overlaps with this candidate.
Prize-eligible theorists such as Bernevig are outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, delivered fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opened clock-based tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. It is a precision measurement of exceptional clarity.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye brought it to the highest accuracy; both are clear. Hall and Hänsch were previously honoured for the frequency comb, which supplies context but not credit overlap.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple laboratories and already used in international comparisons. Redefinition of the second has not yet happened, but the physics itself is established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will see this as an enabling technology advance more than a discovery.
Others who contributed to optical clocks (for example Ludlow, Ovsiannikov) are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the twistronics field and a tunable platform for correlated physics. This is a clear opening of a new regime.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key prediction in 2011, Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators the 2018 experiments. Cory Dean and others contributed related moire results. The three credited names give a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally reproduced widely in under a decade, but the microscopic nature of the superconductivity and correlated states remains debated, so the interpretation is not yet fully settled and timing may be early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism for the superconductivity is still contested.
Possible premature recognition relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal and realisation of the superfluid-to-Mott transition and later quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices created a controllable platform for many-body quantum physics, with lasting impact on condensed matter and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and others proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, with Greiner and Bloch carrying out the experiment. Jaksch is not in the supplied names, and Zoller also appears in B009 and B025, so allocation across candidates needs care.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature, with many laboratories running comparable machines. Some have already been recognised through the ultracold-gas Nobel prizes, which leaves a risk of overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 prize and with other candidates involving Cirac and Zoller.
Missing credit for Jaksch and others who proposed the lattice realisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources opened neutrino astronomy as a genuine new window. The discovery is important and well documented, though outside my own area, where I defer to colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, Karle was a central figure in its construction and analysis. A large collaboration and AMANDA predecessors complicate individual attribution, and the supplied pair is a reasonable but incomplete configuration.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established, and source identification is still growing, so interpretation is stable at the level of discovery while individual source associations remain evolving.
uncertainties: I am outside my expertise and defer to colleagues in astroparticle physics.
Collaboration-scale credit makes the attribution uncertain.
